source_text: sententiae meae pars falsissima est, qua dixi: Nuptiarum bonum malo originali, quod inde trahitur, non potest accusari Quando adulteri gignunt, nascitur homo de virtute seminum, non de turpitudine flagitiorum Si malum inde trahitur, accusari potest, excusari non potest
pass_a_gloss: Of-the-position my pars falsissima is, where dixi: of-marriages good to-evil originali, that/which from-there to-be-drawn, not is-able accusari when adulteri gignunt, is-born human-being about/from by-virtue of-seeds, not about/from turpitudine flagitiorum if evil from-there to-be-drawn, accusari is-able, excusari not is-able.

lemmas.lexica: LS nuptiae=nuptials; Blaise Christian marriage good
LS malum; Blaise malum naturale vs malum voluntatis

pass_b_english: When adulterers conceive a child, a human being is born from the power of the seed, not from the shamefulness of the wrongdoing.
The most false part of [his] position is the statement: “The goodness of marriage cannot be accused on account of the original evil derived from it.”
If evil is derived from it, it can be accused and cannot be excused.
Every cause of evil is without good.

choices.why: Julian defends marriage as God's work against the charge that generation transmits sin.
Keep Julian's good-of-nature vs good-of-will contrast; do not baptize as 'grace'.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
